hints: Use logarithm laws to turn the equation into an algebraic equation, while keeping the logarithm domains valid.
Rewrite $3\ln x$ as $\ln(x^3)$ and combine the right-hand logarithms before removing $\ln$.
Solve the resulting equation $3(x^3-3)=x^3$, then check that $x>0$ and $x^3-3>0$ before rounding.
walkthrough:
Apply the power property of logarithms, $k\ln x = \ln(x^k)$, to rewrite the term $3\ln x$:
$$3\ln x = \ln(x^3)$$
Substitute this into the equation:
$$\ln(x^3 - 3) = \ln(x^3) - \ln 3$$

Apply the quotient rule of logarithms, $\ln A - \ln B = \ln\left(\dfrac{A}{B}\right)$, to combine the terms on the right-hand side:
$$\ln(x^3 - 3) = \ln\left(\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right)$$

Exponentiate both sides (or equate the arguments of the one-to-one logarithmic function) to remove the logarithms:
$$x^3 - 3 = \dfrac{x^3}{3}$$

Multiply both sides by $3$ to eliminate the fraction:
$$3(x^3 - 3) = x^3$$
$$3x^3 - 9 = x^3$$

Rearrange to collect all terms in $x^3$ on one side:
$$3x^3 - x^3 = 9$$
$$2x^3 = 9$$
$$x^3 = \dfrac{9}{2} = 4.5$$

Take the cube root of both sides to isolate $x$:
$$x = \sqrt[3]{4.5} = (4.5)^{\frac{1}{3}}$$

Evaluate the cube root numerically:
$$x \approx 1.65096 \dots$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives:
$$x = 1.65$$
(Checking validity in original logarithms: for $x \approx 1.65$, $x > 0$ and $x^3 - 3 = 4.5 - 3 = 1.5 > 0$, so both arguments are strictly positive.)
